messages:
sam: quick follow-up from my perf dives this morning re: continuous-batching coalesce window shape vs eviction patterns. ran a few targeted microbench experiments and wanted to share numbers + propose next steps.

marta: great, curious what you measured. did you vary arrival distributions?

sam: yep 3 distributions: steady (poisson lambda=120 req/s), spiky (bursts of 500req/s for 10s every 60s), and long-tail (heavy-tailed interarrivals). looked at p50/p95/p99 gen latency, tokens/sec, and CPU/GPU utilization.

chen: nice. what window shapes did you compare?

sam: fixed (6ms), fixed (12ms), exponential backoff (start 2ms, mult 1.8 up to 64ms), adaptive-watermark (target headroom + dynamic backoff based on queue depth). eviction: LRU (by batch age), and headroom-threshold (evict lower-priority queues when free_mem_pct < threshold).

alex: can you paste the config you used?

sam: sure:
```
coalesce_window:
  kind: exponential
  start_ms: 2
  multiplier: 1.8
  max_ms: 64
eviction:
  mode: headroom_threshold
  headroom_pct: 0.15
  protect_short_lived: true
priority_policy: tenant_fairness
```

sam: results (spiky workload, 16-core node, single GPU):
- fixed 6ms + LRU: p50 9ms, p95 42ms, p99 160ms, throughput 86% of baseline, saw GPU stalls during bursts
- fixed 12ms + LRU: p50 12ms, p95 65ms, p99 300ms, throughput 92% but long tail worse
- exponential + LRU: p50 8ms, p95 35ms, p99 120ms, throughput 94%
- exponential + headroom: p50 9ms, p95 28ms, p99 80ms, throughput 97% (best tail behavior)

rachel: interesting that headroom evict improved p99 a lot. is that because it prioritizes younger/bursting batches?

sam: basically. headroom eviction preferentially sheds capacity from lower-priority/fairness lanes earlier which keeps hot lanes fast. LRU alone ends up evicting older batches that sometimes include active long-lived streams causing requeue thrash.

chen: did you see any fairness regressions for noisy tenants? headroom could starve small tenants during sustained bursts.

sam: good catch — with headroom_pct=0.15 we saw one noisy tenant take 60% of GPU cycles in the spiky test. adding a per-tenant min-guarantee (10% of slots) fixed it but reduced peak throughput marginally.

marta: what about adaptive-watermark? how complex was the control loop?

sam: adaptive used EWMA of queue depth + recent batch completion times to set a coalesce target. performed well in long-tail workload (p99 down ~40% vs fixed) but the loop needs damping to avoid oscillation. saw oscillation when EWMA alpha too high (0.6) — settled with alpha=0.2 and a 50ms cooldown.

alex: do we have traces/graphs for these runs?

sam: uploaded flamegraphs + traces to the perf bucket, link: https://perf.internal/reports/2480005555-coalesce (internal only). included short replay scripts.

ops-bot: deployment-note: experiment cluster x-rt-3 currently running exp config; will auto-cleanup after 2h.

rachel: what about implementation surface area for runtime? changing eviction from LRU to headroom sounds like a refactor across queue manager and admission. estimated scope?

sam: roughly: (1) add headroom signal in allocator (~200 LOC), (2) eviction hook in queue manager (~150 LOC), (3) telemetry + flags (~100 LOC), (4) tests + backward compat (~150 LOC). dev estimate 3-4d to get a safe canary.

marta: any concerns about increased code complexity vs maintenance burden?

sam: yes — the headroom logic is small but its interactions with tenant guarantees & preemption need careful tests. I'm leaning to implement as an optional eviction plugin behind a feature flag and run A/B tests vs current LRU.

chen: what metrics should we track in the A/B? p99, fairness (max/min throughput per tenant), eviction rate, requeue rate, and tail-kv-cache-misses.

alex: also track burst recovery time (time to return to baseline latency after a burst) and GPU occupancy variance.

rachel: if we ship headroom as plugin, we should add a telemetry event for eviction decisions (why evicted, headroom_pct at eviction, victim tenant). keep payload small.

sam: agree. proposed next steps:
1) Sam to land headroom plugin PR behind flag (WIP).
2) Add per-tenant min-guarantee and config knobs.
3) Run 48h A/B on staging with spiky + long-tail replay.
4) If stable, canary roll to one dedicated cluster and monitor metrics above.

marta: sounds good. schedule a 30m sync to review PR and telemetry schema?

sam: yes — propose tomorrow 10:30am.

alex: I'll pair-review the PR and help set up the replay harness.

chen: I'll draft the telemetry schema and alerts for fairness regressions.

rachel: +1. also add an ops-runbook note in case eviction plugin causes unexpected thrash.

sam: thanks all — will post PR link shortly. :thumbsup:
